{"self_assessment": "Impact: I put the fish sketch on the pad in the first minutes, giving the table one shared plan to build from. It had a single start at the nose, a line over the back, a line under the belly and a forked tail, drawn as smooth curves so one push could run through it. Everything the table built followed from that sketch, and the whole run was standing well before time was up. At the last check, all 131 dominoes were connected to the start, with only the two tail tips open.

Execution: I checked the work closely and often. I inspected the run five times (nose split, back, tail junction, upper fork) to confirm what the start would knock over. When I saw the middle of the back doubled up, I traced it, confirmed it was still connected, and left it alone rather than risk a bump. I also pushed for hands-off once the run was complete, to protect it before the push.

Collaboration: I kept the table's work organized. I suggested splitting the top line so people weren't crowded at the nose, with one person jumping to the middle of the back. I said where I would work, so we stayed out of each other's way. I replied promptly to teammates' questions and requests to check specific areas, and I backed the group's decision to stop touching the table.

Leadership: I helped set direction early by backing the fish and getting the sketch up quickly. I then helped keep the roles clear as the lines grew toward the tail. When the top line was the slow one, I spotted it and proposed a way to speed it up. Near the end I helped the table settle into a calm, no-touch finish.

I believe my share of the table's result is about 30%, mainly the sketch, the coordination and the repeated checks.", "my_share_percent": 30}
